newsitem.title: USA: New Hampshire death row dog's life is spared.
newsitem.headline: New Hampshire death row dog's life is spared.

text.p: After six months on a veterinarian's death row, worldwide publicity and repeated court action, a 3-year-old dog that killed a rooster and became a cause celebre was spared on Tuesday from execution.

The black Labrador named Prince will not be executed but instead will be banished from Portsmouth. Under a deal worked out with prosecutors, Prince's owners, Margaret Kristiansen and her son, Jeffrey, 5, agreed to find the dog a new home outside city limits in exchange for dropping all charges.
"I don't think he will be leaving the state but he will be leaving the city," a weeping Kristiansen told reporters outside the courthouse in Portsmouth. "I'm going to find him a good home."
Her lawyer, Peter Marsh of Concord, said, "Margaret fought to save Prince's life and today she succeeded ... She put the dog first."

Prince's execution was required under Portsmouth's strict vicious-dog ordinance, which permits no exceptions. He was labeled a vicious dog after escaping from his pen into a neighbour's chicken yard and killing a rooster last May.
He was supposed to have been kept in the pen unless he was restrained on a chain, but he escaped twice. Under the law, any vicious dog that escapes twice must be destroyed.
But when people learned of Prince's fate, hundreds offered to adopt him, the governor said she would consider pardoning him and the town held a candlelight vigil for the animal.
